did_you_know.text: Mount Seir is identified with the mountainous region of Edom, south and east of the Dead Sea. Turning north therefore marks a change in direction after a long stay in the area.
The command to buy food and water shows that the journey also involved trade with local residents, not only reliance on their own supplies.
The verse presents the forty years in the wilderness not only as a time of hardship, but also as a period in which the people survived without lacking essential needs.
The Arabah is a geographic rift extending from the southern Dead Sea toward the Gulf of Aqaba. Eilat and Ezion-geber were important points near the gulf’s northern end.
The name Emim is probably related to the Hebrew word for “terror,” perhaps reflecting the impression this people made on its neighbors.

The verse compares Edom’s possession of Seir with Israel’s possession of its land. It presents changes in control of territory as a process that occurred among different peoples, not only among Israel.
The journey from Kadesh-barnea to the Zered Valley lasted thirty-eight years. The number emphasizes the transition from the generation that left Egypt to a new generation prepared to enter the land.

Caphtor, the homeland of the Caphtorim, is often identified with Crete, though the identification is not completely certain. The verse preserves traditions about peoples who reached the Gaza region from distant places.
The Arnon Valley is generally identified with Wadi Mujib in modern Jordan, which flows into the Dead Sea. It served as an important natural boundary east of the Jordan.
Before the war with Sihon, Moses sent messengers with a peaceful proposal. This shows an attempt to cross the land by agreement before the situation turned into war.
The biblical term herem describes a total destruction devoted to God in a wartime setting. It is a religious and legal term from the biblical world, not merely a description of military victory.
The area described stretches from Aroer on the bank of the Arnon to Gilead. Gilead is a mountainous region east of the Jordan, so this refers to a broad part of Transjordan.
